## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | US stock tickers; None, the default, for no ticker filter (`dm.ALL` is refused). | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and the rows of each one you delete leave the table. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `start` | The earliest publication time; `poll()` needs it or a `limit`. | The first day or moment of the range. A date (text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`) means the day in the market's time zone: New York for stocks, options, and indices; UTC for forex and crypto; for futures, the trading session that ends that day. An instant is an exact time: a Python `datetime` with a time zone, a `pandas.Timestamp`, a `numpy.datetime64`, a Deephaven `Instant` or `ZonedDateTime`, or Deephaven time text such as `"2025-06-02T09:30 ET"`. Give `start` and `end` as two dates or two instants. A `datetime` without a time zone raises `ValueError`, and a calendar-date field, such as an ex-dividend date, takes dates only. |
| `end` | The end of the range. | The last day, or the moment the range stops, in the same form as `start`. A date includes its whole day, so `start="2025-06-02", end="2025-06-02"` reads all of June 2; an instant is excluded. Leave it out to read through now; a list dataset then sends Massive no end, so it also returns records still to come, such as dividends announced but not yet paid. |
| `sort` | Massive's field to sort by, such as `"published"`. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | The direction of `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Such as `{"channels_any_of": ["earnings"]}`. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The ticker the request named that the row lists in `Tickers`: a row that lists several of the named tickers appears once for each, so an article about AAPL and MSFT read for both is listed under each. A request that named one ticker gives it to every row. Null when the call named no ticker, and on a row that lists none of a request's named tickers. | REST |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's primary time, as an Instant. From REST `published`: "The timestamp (formatted as an ISO 8601 timestamp) when the news article was originally published." | REST |
| `Author` | String | The name of the journalist or entity that authored the news article. | REST |
| `BenzingaId` | long | The identifier used by Benzinga for this record. | REST |
| `Body` | String | The full text content of the news article. | REST |
| `Channels` | String[] | A list of categories or topics that the article belongs to (e.g., 'News', 'Price Target'). | REST |
| `Images` | String[] | A list of images associated with the article. | REST |
| `LastUpdated` | Instant | The timestamp (formatted as an ISO 8601 timestamp) when the news article was last updated in the system. | REST |
| `Tags` | String[] | A list of tags that describe the themes or content of the article. | REST |
| `Teaser` | String | A short summary or lead-in to the news article's content. | REST |
| `Tickers` | String[] | A list of stock or crypto tickers mentioned in the article. | REST |
| `Title` | String | The headline of the news article. | REST |
| `Url` | String | The direct link to the source of the news article. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
